name: QXO, INC.
moat_justification: Real and growing procurement/branch scale in a fragmented industry, bought entirely with raised capital in 15 months; distribution has no structural switching costs, equally scaled rivals exist (ABC Supply, Home Depot-owned SRS), and the acquired business has not yet produced a positive-ROIC filed year (FY2025 roic_proxy -1.9%, TTM operating margin -3.4%, gross margin 23-24%).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 391.2%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

IRR_AT_FLOOR: implied IRR sits within 0.5pp of terminal growth 2.5% (super_bear, bear, base, weighted) — a perpetuity growing at g has an IRR above g at any price, so the model cannot express a return below ~2.5%; this price is beyond the model's range and the expected return is 'at most ~3.0%', not the recorded figure
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 0.06 vs 3-yr median 0.25 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 0.2% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.0x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 62.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Jacobs rollup with real scale but no filed earnings power yet, moat 4/10 — TTM owner's earnings $0.018/share vs a $10.86 price (weighted IRR at the ~3% floor, IV@15% $0.29); clears 15% only at $0.29 on filed numbers, so the price bets on unfiled TopBuild earnings and execution.
moat_for: Largest roofing distributor in North America via Beacon; pro-forma #2 publicly traded building products distributor (>$18B revenue) after TopBuild — procurement leverage in an $800B fragmented industry
Branch density and pro-contractor job-site presence across roofing, waterproofing, insulation and complementary products
Brad Jacobs' demonstrated rollup playbook (XPO, United Rentals) — disciplined dealmaking and operational lift
moat_against: Distribution is structurally low-moat: local relationships, no switching costs, customers multi-source
ABC Supply (private) and Home Depot-owned SRS Distribution are equally or better scaled without rollup premiums
ROIC evidence is negative: FY2025 roic_proxy -1.9%, TTM operating income -$337.6M, gross margin 23.0% FY2025 / 24.0% TTM — commodity distribution economics
Tech/AI playbook unproven in this vertical; three mega-deals (Beacon, Kodiak, TopBuild) in 15 months is an unmatched integration load
39% of Q2 2026 sales are residential roofing — hostage to soft housing volumes
